# difficulty

> A compiled language that writes like a more pleasant C: C-like syntax, Python-like simplicity,
> one way to write each thing, no silent fallbacks, diagnostics that say how to fix them.
> Covers parts 1, 2a (values, methods), 2b (errors, tests), 2c (numbers, lists, maps, text,
> io), 2d (function literals, blocks). Binding: docs/spec.md; codes are rule numbers (R1–R31) or lexical/syntax codes (L, S).

## Tools

```
dif check [--json] main.dif    # syntax, names, types; one JSON object per line with --json
dif run main.dif               # compile via C11 and run
dif build main.dif -o prog     # native program (needs cc, gcc or clang; or set CC)
dif test [path] [filter] [--json]   # run the `test` blocks, see part 2b
```

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 diagnostics (or an error from `void!E main`), 2 usage error, no C compiler, a
panic, 3 internal error (C compiler rejects the generated C: a bug in dif).
A diagnostic: `main.dif:3:11: error[R9]: condition is int, not bool` plus `hint: …`.
Columns count characters. One diagnostic per mistake; fix the first, rerun.

## A program

```dif
const int LIMIT = 10

int square(int n) {
    return n * n
}

void main() {
    int total = 0
    for int i in range(1, LIMIT) {
        if i % 2 == 0 {
            continue
        }
        total += square(i)
    }
    print("sum of odd squares below {LIMIT}: {total}")
}
```

- A program is functions and `const` declarations, in any order; it starts in `void main()`.
- Statements only inside functions. No global variables, only global `const`.

## Rules of part 1

**Lines.** A statement ends at the end of its line. No `;`. A line continues when it ends
with a binary operator, `=`, an assignment operator or `,`, inside `( )` and `[ ]`,
or when the next line starts with `.`. Two statements on one line: R3.

**Blocks.** Always `{ }`, the `{` on the line of its header, `} else {` on one line.
No parentheses needed around conditions. `else if`, never `elif`.

**Declarations name their type first** and always have a value (R2):
`int n = 0`, `bool done = false`, `str name = "dif"`, `const int K = 3`.
Function: `int add(int a, int b) { … }`; no return value: `void`.
Loop variables too: `for int i in range(n)`.

**Names (R4).** A name lives until the end of its block, including inner blocks, and is
never declared again there (no shadowing, also not as parameter or loop variable).
Sibling blocks may reuse a name. `const` is never assigned. Predefined names and keywords cannot
be names; `ok err none some test` are reserved. Names use ASCII letters, digits and `_`.

**Types (R8).** `int` (64 bit), `bool`, `str`, `void`; more in part 2c. Types never mix:
`"a" + 1` is an error; build text with interpolation `"{a}{b}"`.

| operator | operands | result |
|---|---|---|
| `+ - * / %` `+% -% *%` `& \| ^ << >>` | int, int | int |
| `-x` `~x` | int | int |
| `+` | str, str | str |
| `== !=` | same type | bool |
| `< <= > >=` | int or str (both the same) | bool |
| `&& \|\| !` | bool | bool (R9) |

**Conditions are bool (R9).** `while n {` is an error; write `while n != 0 {`.

**Precedence**, weakest first: `??` · `||` · `&&` · comparisons · `|` · `^` · `&` ·
shifts · `+ -` · `* / %` · unary `- ! ~` · call/index/field. Bit operators bind tighter
than comparisons: `x & 1 == 0` means `(x & 1) == 0`.
Not allowed: chains `a < b < c` (S2, write `a < b && b < c`) and `&&` mixed with `||`
without parentheses (S3).

**Loops (R11).** `for int i in range(n)` (0 … n-1), `for int i in range(a, b)` (a … b-1),
bounds evaluated once; `while cond`; `break`, `continue` only inside loops.
`range` only appears as the source of a `for`.

**Results are used (R13).** A call of a function that returns a value, used as a
statement, is an error; use the value or discard it explicitly: `_ = f(x)`.
`print(x)` returns nothing and is a statement.

**Numbers (R29, R14).** Overflow of `+ - *` and unary `-` aborts; `+% -% *%` wrap
modulo 2^64. `/` rounds toward 0, `%` has the sign of the dividend (`-7 / 2 == -3`,
`-7 % 3 == -1`). Division by 0 and `INT_MIN / -1` abort. Shifts take 0 … 63 places, `>>`
keeps the sign. Operands and arguments are evaluated left to right. Literals: `1_000`,
`0xff`, `0b1010`, no leading zeros. Literals and `const` are computed exactly at compile
time; only the result must fit; a certain abort there (`1 / 0`) is R14.

**Text.** `"…"` on one line. Escapes `\n \t \r \\ \" \{ \} \0 \u{1F600}`.
`{expr}` inserts any int, bool or str; no strings or braces inside `{ }`;
a literal brace is `\{` or `\}`. `print(x)` writes `x` and a newline.

**Abort.** A programming error stops the program with
`panic: integer overflow in + (main.dif:3:15)` on stderr and exit code 2.

```dif snippet
int big = 9223372036854775807
print(big +% 1)
print(-7 / 2)
print(1 << 62)
str s = "a" + "b"
bool same = s == "ab"
print("{s} {same}")
```

```dif panic "division by zero"
int z = 0
print(10 / z)
```

## Part 2a: values, methods, `mut`, `switch`

```dif
struct Point {
    int x
    int y = 0
}

enum Shape {
    Square(int side)
    Rect(int w, int h)
    Dot
}

Point Point.moved(int dx) {
    Point q = self
    q.x += dx
    return q
}

void Point.scale(mut self, int k) {
    self.x *= k
    self.y *= k
}

void shift(mut Point p, int dx) {
    p.x += dx
}

int area(Shape s) {
    switch s {
    case Shape.Square(int side):
        return side * side
    case Shape.Rect(int w, _):
        return w
    case Shape.Dot:
        return 0
    }
}

void main() {
    Point a = Point{x: 1, y: 2}
    Point b = a
    shift(mut b, 5)
    b.scale(2)
    int n = if b.x > 10 { area(Shape.Square(3)) } else { 0 }
    print("{a} {b} {b.moved(1)} {n} {Shape.Rect(3, 4)}")
}
```

Output: `Point{x: 1, y: 2} Point{x: 12, y: 4} Point{x: 13, y: 4} 9 Shape.Rect(3, 4)`

- **`struct` (R5).** One field per line, optional default (`int y = 0`, constants and
  effect-free calls only, evaluated at every literal that omits the field). A literal
  names every field without default, in any order, evaluated left to right:
  `Point{x: 1}`. Assignment, parameters and return copy the value. A type cannot
  contain itself.
- **`enum` (R5).** `enum Seat { Free, Taken }`; variants may carry values
  (`NoSuchSeat(int row, int seat)`). Always written with the type: `Seat.Free`,
  `BookErr.NoSuchSeat(3, 5)`. Values are read only through `switch`.
- **`mut` (R6).** A function that changes an argument takes `mut T p`, the caller writes
  `mut`: `shift(mut b, 5)`; places are variables, fields, elements. R6: a `mut` parameter
  never changed, a change never read afterwards (also to a copy), one place passed
  changeable twice in a call. An argument without `mut` sees the value from before the call.
- **Methods (R7).** `R Type.name(params)`; `self` is the place before the dot; a method that
  changes it takes `mut self` first. `a.scale(2)` needs a variable or field then, no `mut`
  at the call; others work on any expression: `fresh().total()`.
- **`switch` (R10).** Over numbers, `rune`, `str` or `enum`; values are literals, `const`
  names or `E.V`; `case 1, 2:` lists values; bindings `case E.V(int w, _):` (`_` skips).
  No fall-through; `continue` and `return` work inside, `break` not directly. Every variant
  is handled or there is a `default`; over other types `default` is required.
- **`if` as a value (R15).** `str s = if n < 0 { "neg" } else { "pos" }`; `else` is
  required, each branch ends with an expression, or with `return`/`break`/`continue` (one
  branch needs a value); only the chosen branch runs, all values have one type.
- **Equality and text (R28).** `==` compares field by field and by variant; text looks like
  the literal, `str` inside is quoted: `Person{name: "Ada", age: 36}`. `<` does not exist.

```dif error R6
struct Point {
    int x
    int y
}

void shift(mut Point p, int dx) {
    p.x += dx
}

void main() {
    Point b = Point{x: 1, y: 2}
    shift(b, 5)
    print(b)
}
```

## Part 2b: failure in the type, `try`, tests

```dif
enum AgeErr {
    Negative
    TooOld(int n)
}

?int half(int n) {
    if n % 2 != 0 {
        return none
    }
    return n / 2
}

int!AgeErr check_age(int n) {
    if n < 0 {
        return err(AgeErr.Negative)
    }
    return n
}

int!AgeErr double_age(int n) {
    return try check_age(n) * 2
}

void main() {
    print(half(8))
    print(half(7) ?? -1)
    print(double_age(-1))
    switch double_age(4) {
    case ok(int n):
        print("ok {n}")
    case err(AgeErr e):
        print("error {e}")
    }
}
```

Output: `some(4)`, `-1`, `err(AgeErr.Negative)`, `ok 8`

- **Types (R12).** `?T` is a `T` or `none`; `T!E` is a `T` or an error `E` (any type);
  `void!E` is nothing or an error. Success is returned plainly: `return n`; failure is
  `return none` or `return err(AgeErr.Negative)`. `none`, `err(e)` take their type from
  the place they stand in (declaration, argument, `return`, the other side of `==`); alone
  it is R12. `some(x)` is for comparing: `x == some(3)`; `x == 3` is R8. `ok(x)`
  exists only as a pattern.
- **`try x`** (functions and tests only): the value of `x`, or the function returns at
  once with the same error or `none`. `try x or e` runs `e` only on failure and turns the
  error into the function's own type: `e` is such a value, `err(E e): F.V(e)` binds the
  cause (`E` = error type of `x`), or `F.V` alone when that variant holds exactly the
  cause (`try read() or AppErr.Io`); not for `?T`. Another error type without `or` is R12.
  `try` binds like a sign: `try f(a) + try f(b)`; as a statement `try f()`.
- **`a ?? b`**: `a` if it has a value, else `b` (evaluated only then); `a` is `?T` or `T!E`.
- **`switch` (R10)** over `T!E`: `case ok(int n):` and `case err(E e):`; over `?T`:
  `case some(int n):` and `case none:`; `ok` without parentheses for `void!E`; `_` skips the
  value; both forms or a `default` are needed.
- **Use (R13).** A `T!E` or `?T` is always used: `try`, `??`, `switch`, argument,
  `return`, or discarded with `_ = f()`; a bare `f()` statement is R13.
- **Equality and text (R28).** `==` compares `?T` with `?T` and `T!E` with `T!E`;
  text is `some(4)`, `none`, `ok(30)`, `err(AgeErr.Negative)`, `ok` for `void!E`.
- **`void!E main()`**: an error ends the program with `error: <text>` on stderr
  (a `str` unchanged) and exit code 1; a panic is still exit code 2.

```dif fails "HallErr.NoSeat(7)"
enum HallErr {
    NoSeat(int n)
}

void!HallErr book(int n) {
    if n > 5 {
        return err(HallErr.NoSeat(n))
    }
    print("booked {n}")
}

void!HallErr main() {
    try book(3)
    try book(7)
    print("not reached")
}
```

**Tests (R18).** `test "name" { … }` at the top level, checked with `expect(cond)`;
`dif run` and `dif build` skip them. `test "name" panics "text" { … }` passes only with a
panic whose message contains `text`. `try` in a test fails the test with `try failed: …`.

`dif test [path] [filter] [--json]` runs every test in its own process; `path` is a file or
directory (default `.`), `filter` selects tests whose name contains it. A failure shows the
reason, the value of every non-literal operand, and what the test printed. Exit code 0 all
passed, 1 a test failed or none was selected, 2 files do not compile. `--json`: docs/spec.md R18.

```dif test
int add(int a, int b) {
    return a + b
}

test "addition" {
    expect(add(2, 3) == 5)
}

test "wrong sum" {
    int a = 2
    expect(a + 2 == 5)
}
```

```
ok   main.dif:5 test "addition"
FAIL main.dif:9 test "wrong sum"
    main.dif:11:5: expect failed: a + 2 == 5
        a + 2 = 4
test result: 1 passed, 1 failed
```

## Part 2c: numbers, text, lists, maps, `io`

```dif
use std.io

struct Task {
    str title
    []str tags = []
}

f64 mean([]int xs) {
    int sum = 0
    for int x in xs {
        sum += x
    }
    return f64(sum) / f64(xs.len())
}

void!io.IoErr main() {
    []int xs = [3, 1, 2]
    xs.push(4)
    xs.sort()
    map[str]int counts = {}
    for str w in "to be or to be".split(" ") {
        counts[w] = (counts[w] ?? 0) + 1
    }
    Task t = Task{title: " Write "}
    t.tags.push("doc")
    t.title = t.title.trim().upper()
    print("{xs} {xs[0]} {counts} {t}")
    print("{mean(xs):.2f} {u8(200) +% 100} {int((2.7).round())}")
    for str line in try io.lines() {
        print(line.len())
    }
}
```

Output: `[1, 2, 3, 4] 1 {"to": 2, "be": 2, "or": 1} Task{title: "WRITE", tags: ["doc"]}`, `2.50 44 3`

- **Numbers (R8, R29).** `int i8 i16 i32 u8 u16 u32 u64 f64 rune`; they never mix, also not
  `int` and `i32`. A literal takes the type of its place (`u8 b = 200`, `f64 x = 3`); a float
  literal only `f64`. Each width aborts on overflow; `+% -% *%` wrap. `f64` is IEEE (`1.0 / 0.0`
  is `inf`, `NaN != NaN`, `%` is fmod); text is the shortest digits that read back (`22.5`,
  `1e21`); `{x:.2f}`, `{x:g}` format only `f64`.
- **Conversions (R31).** `T(x)` is exact or aborts (`u8(300)`: `300 does not fit in u8`;
  `int(2.5)`: `2.5 is not an exact int`): between ints, `f64(n)`, `int(x.round())`, `rune(n)`,
  `str(r)`. `n.to_u8()` gives `?u8`. Nothing converts by itself, `str` and numbers never.
- **`str` and `rune`.** `'a'` is a `rune`; no `s[i]`: `s.slice(a, b)` counts bytes, `s.runes()`,
  `len()`. Methods: `split lines trim trim_start trim_end lower upper contains starts_with
  ends_with find replace repeat parse_int parse_f64 is_empty`; `rune`: `is_digit is_letter is_space`.
- **Lists `[]T` and arrays `[N]T` (R5).** Values: `ys = xs` copies, a write to one never shows
  in the other (copy-on-write inside, `push` is O(1)). `xs[i]` is checked (abort, R14);
  `xs[i] = v`, `xs[i].f = v`, `normalize(mut xs[i])` write. Methods: `len is_empty push pop insert
  remove first last contains index_of count sort reverse swap slice join`; `pop first last index_of`
  give `?T`. `[]`/`{}` need a typed place. `repeat(0, n)`. Arrays have no
  `push pop insert remove`.
- **Maps `map[K]V` (R30).** `m[k]` is `?V`, `m[k] = v` sets; `m[k] += 1` is R8, use `m.add(k, 1)`.
  `len has remove add keys values`; entries keep insertion order. `m[k]` is not a place: no
  `m[k].f = v`, no `mut m[k]` (R30).
- **Loops (R11).** `for T x in xs`, `for int i, T x in xs`, `for K k, V v in m` run over the
  value at the start; writes to `xs` in the body do not show. `for T x in try rs` unpacks a
  list of `T!E` like `try`.
- **`io`, `os` (R16).** `use std.io` / `use std.os` first in the file. `io.lines()` (only as
  `for str l in try io.lines()`), `io.read_line()`, `io.read_file(p)`, `io.write_file(p, s)`,
  `io.read_lines(p)`, `io.write_lines(p, ls)`, `io.eprint(x)`, `os.args()`, `os.env(name)`, `os.exit(code)`. Errors are `io.IoErr`:
  `NotFound(path)`, `NoPermission(path)`, `InvalidUtf8(path)`, `Other(path, reason)`. A line
  loses a trailing `\r`. A `str` is always valid UTF-8.
- **Text (R28).** `[1, 2]`, `["a"]`, `{"k": 1}`, `['a']`: `str` and `rune` inside are quoted;
  `==` works on all, `<` only on numbers, `rune`, `str`.
- **Aborts (R14).** Index or slice out of range, `T(x)` inexact, negative `repeat`, empty `split`
  separator, `NaN` as a map key, two `mut` elements with the same index, `assert(false)`.
  `out of memory` has no line.

```dif panic "index 3 out of bounds for length 3"
[]int xs = [1, 2, 3]
int i = 3
print(xs[i])
```

## Part 2d: function literals and blocks (R26)

- **Function type** `R(T1, mut T2)`: only as the type of a parameter (`void times(int n, void() body)`,
  `int sum([]int xs, int(int) f)`); elsewhere R26. A `?` or `!E` before `(` belongs to `R`.
  In the body such a name is only called (`f(x)`, `mut` where the type says) or passed on.
- **Literal** `R(T x) { … }`: only as an argument of a call, else R26. Detected as an argument that
  starts `X (`, then `)`, `mut` or `T name`, and `{` on the line of the `)`. `Name() { … }` is a literal
  if `Name` is a type, a call with a block if it is a function.
- **Block** `{ … }` right after `)` of a call (same line): the last argument, a literal without
  parameters; its parameter must be `R()` (else R26). `times(3) { print("hi") }`. Nothing follows
  the closing `}`. In a header the `{` ends the head: write `if (ready() { … }) {`, or the literal.
- **Named function or variant constructor** as argument: `mapped(xs, triple)`, `shapes(xs, Shape.Box)`;
  the type must match exactly (R8). Any other use of a function name is R26.
- **Values, not places.** A literal copies each outside name it uses when its call evaluates its
  arguments (counted, no deep copy) and never changes anything outside: a change to a captured name
  is R6 (`return the value or use a for loop`). Handles stay the same handle. `return` and `try`
  end only the literal; `break`/`continue` do not see an outer loop (R11).
- **Effect (R13).** A call has an effect if its function or one of its literals does (`print`, a call
  with effect); `any_of(xs, bool(int x) { print(x) … })` is a valid statement, a pure one is R13.

```dif
int sum_with([]int xs, int(int) f) {
    int total = 0
    for int x in xs {
        total += f(x)
    }
    return total
}

void times(int n, void() body) {
    for int i in range(n) {
        body()
    }
}

void main() {
    int factor = 10
    times(2) {
        print(sum_with([1, 2], int(int x) { return x * factor }))
    }
}
```

## Habits from other languages and their fixes

| written | code | write instead |
|---|---|---|
| `var x = 5`, `let x = 5`, `auto x = 5` | R2 | `int x = 5` |
| `def f():`, `fn f(a: int) -> int`, `function f()` | R2 | `int f(int a) { … }` |
| `for i in range(10)` | R2 | `for int i in range(10)` |
| `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)` | R11 | `for int i in range(n)` |
| `elif`, `elsif` | R3 | `} else if … {` |
| `while n {` | R9 | `while n != 0 {` |
| `"n = " + n` | R8 | `"n = {n}"` |
| `f(x)` result unused | R13 | `int y = f(x)` or `_ = f(x)` |
| `shift(b, 5)` when `shift` takes `mut` | R6 | `shift(mut b, 5)` |
| `case Free:` in a `switch` over an enum | R10 | `case Seat.Free:` |
| assignment to an undeclared name | R2 | declare it: `int x = …` |

```dif error R2
void main() {
    var x = 5
    print(x)
}
```

```dif error R13
int square(int n) {
    return n * n
}

void main() {
    square(3)
}
```

## Limits

Nesting deeper than 256 levels or 1024 operators in one expression is S1: split it.

## Not yet

`filter`/`map`/`sort_by`/`any`/`all` on lists, storing function values, own modules, C import,
handles, sharing: later parts (PLAN.md); using them is an error that says so.
